nations.name: Paiwan
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range across Pingtung and Taitung counties, Taiwan

facts.text: About 102,730 Paiwan people were counted in January 2020, living in the southern mountains of Pingtung and Taitung.
The Ravar branch of the Paiwan is known for outstanding carving and pottery.

nations.name: Wanniyala-Aetto
nations.lands: Eastern Sri Lanka, including the Maduru Oya area

facts.text: In 1983, 51,468 hectares of Wanniyala-Aetto customary land were declared the Maduru Oya National Park.
Their own name, Wanniyala-Aetto, means forest dwellers, and their ancestors lived on the island long before the Sinhalese and the Tamils arrived.

nations.name: Tsou
nations.lands: Alishan Township in Chiayi County, plus Nantou and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Tsou homeland centres on Alishan Township in Chiayi County, southwest of Yushan in central Taiwan.
The Tsou population was 6,702 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mentawai
nations.lands: The Mentawai Islands, including Siberut, off West Sumatra, Indonesia

facts.text: On Siberut, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1981, Mentawai communities use the forest with care, guided by traditional knowledge.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

facts.text: Siberut, home to many Mentawai communities, is the largest of the four Mentawai Islands west of Sumatra.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

nations.name: Lumad
nations.lands: Mindanao, Philippines

facts.text: Lumad is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Mindanao, among them the Manobo, Subanon, Mandaya, Talandig and Teduray.
Lumad advocacy, with allies, helped write two important provisions into the 1987 Philippine Constitution.

nations.name: Khasi
nations.lands: Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, and nearby Bangladesh

facts.text: The Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council has a wing that oversees the Elakas, the traditional Khasi states.

source.title: General Administration Department and Elaka Administration

facts.text: Apart from Shillong's municipality and cantonment, all of Meghalaya is governed under the Sixth Schedule, the only northeast state where this is so.

nations.name: Bunun
nations.lands: Both sides of the Central Mountain Range in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Bunun live higher in the mountains than any other Indigenous people in Taiwan, mostly between 500 and 1,500 metres.
About 59,536 Bunun people were counted in January 2020, with homes in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung.

nations.name: Tamang
nations.lands: Hills around the Kathmandu Valley and central Nepal

facts.text: The Tamang are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tamang is the mother tongue of about 4.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Akha
nations.lands: Northern Thailand, eastern Myanmar and northern Laos

facts.text: The Akha are one of more than 20 highland Indigenous peoples of northern Thailand.

nations.name: Saisiyat
nations.lands: Hsinchu and Miaoli counties in northwestern Taiwan

facts.text: The Saisiyat live in northwestern Taiwan, in Hsinchu County and Miaoli County on either side of Ngangihaw mountain.
The Saisiyat population was 6,730 in January 2020.

nations.name: Truku
nations.lands: Xiulin, Wanrong and Zhuoxi townships in Hualien County, Taiwan

facts.text: The Truku were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2004.
About 32,333 Truku people were counted in January 2020, mostly in Hualien County.

nations.name: Sediq
nations.lands: Mountain areas of Nantou and Hualien in central Taiwan

facts.text: Three subgroups make up the Sediq, each with its own group identity: Seediq Tgdaya, Sediq Toda and Sejiq Truku.
About 10,452 Sediq people were counted in January 2020, mostly in the mountains of Nantou and Hualien.

nations.name: Bhil
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, India

facts.text: India's government names the Bhil among the tribal peoples whose movements strengthened the country's freedom struggle.

source.title: Cabinet approves declaration of 15th November as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
source.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India

nations.name: Marma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh

facts.text: Together, the Chakma, Marma and Tripura make up about 90 percent of the Indigenous peoples of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Yakthung
nations.lands: Limbuwan in the eastern hills of Nepal, including Taplejung, Panchthar, Terhathum and Ilam, plus Jhapa, Morang and Sunsari, with communities in Sikkim and Darjeeling, India

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 84.5 percent of Yakthung people reported Limbu as their mother tongue, a language with its own script, Sirijanga.

source.title: लिम्बु (Limbu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Limbu, alongside Maithili, as an official language of Province 1 in eastern Nepal.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tharu
nations.lands: The Terai plains of southern Nepal, and neighbouring India

facts.text: The Tharu are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tharu is the mother tongue of about 5.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Kurukh
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal in India, with communities in Assam, Bangladesh and Nepal

facts.text: Odisha counted 358,112 Kurukh (Oraon) people in 2011; many farm and practice crafts such as carpentry, rope making and weaving date palm leaf mats.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Oraon
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: Twelve to thirty Kurukh villages join in a Parha council, where members of each village council meet under a Parha chief.

source.title: Oraon
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Thao
nations.lands: Ita Thao Village by Sun Moon Lake and Dapinglin, Nantou County, Taiwan

facts.text: Thao people live mainly in Ita Thao Village in Yuchi Township and in Dapinglin, Shuili Township, both in Nantou County. They numbered about 817 in January 2020.
Thao oral history tells of ancestors who followed a white deer to Sun Moon Lake and found a fertile place full of fish.

nations.name: Pinuyumayan
nations.lands: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain, Taiwan

facts.text: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain are the heart of Pinuyumayan life today.
About 14,517 Pinuyumayan people were counted in January 2020, and many have moved from eastern Taiwan to cities, where they are active in many fields.

nations.name: Santal
nations.lands: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and nearby states of India, northwest Bangladesh, and Nepal

facts.text: On 25 December 2025, India's Constitution was released in the Santali language, written in the Ol Chiki script.

source.title: President of India releases the Constitution of India in the Santhali language

facts.text: Santali, the Santal language, is one of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of India's Constitution.

source.title: Languages Included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
source.publisher: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, India

nations.name: Munda
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Bihar in India, with communities in Bangladesh

facts.text: Mundari has its own script, known in the community as Mundari Bani; a version reformed in 2008 by Munda community bodies is in the Unicode Standard.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Munda call their dance durang and their song susun, and both women and men dance at social events and seasonal festivals.

source.title: Munda
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Ho
nations.lands: Kolhan region of Jharkhand and northern Odisha, with communities in West Bengal and Bihar, India

facts.text: In Odisha, Ho farmers grow paddy, maize and ragi, tend kitchen gardens, and gather mushrooms, mahua and greens from the forest.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Ho
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: The Ho language has its own recently devised alphabet, Warang Citi, which is encoded in the Unicode Standard and used by a yearly and a biweekly publication.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

nations.name: Kanakanavu
nations.lands: Namaxia District, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: On June 26, 2014, Taiwan's government recognized the Kanakanavu as an independent people, the 16th on the official list.
Some Kanakanavu people understand their name as people living in a forest of Taiwan giant bamboo.

nations.name: Rai
nations.lands: Majh Kirat, also called Khambuwan, in the middle hills of eastern Nepal between the Dudh Koshi and Arun rivers, plus Jhapa, Morang, Sunsari and the Kathmandu Valley

facts.text: The Kirat Rai Yayokkha, founded in 1990, works to unite Nepal's diverse Rai communities and to promote Rai languages, arts and literature.
The Rai are a multilingual people: the Kirat Rai Yayokkha has registered 26 Rai language groups, among them Bantawa, Chamling and Kulung.

source.title: राई (Rai)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Rukai
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung, Taiwan

facts.text: About 13,465 Rukai people were counted in January 2020, living in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung.
For the Rukai, the lily stands for purity and courage, and the right to wear lily ornaments sits at the heart of their culture.

nations.name: Gond
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Odisha and neighboring states of central India

facts.text: Masaram Gondi, a script created in 1918 by Munshi Mangal Singh Masaram of Madhya Pradesh to write the Gondi language, is still used today in handwritten and printed materials.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Gond painting, mostly made in Patangarh village in Dindori district, gained worldwide recognition after shows in Tokyo and Paris and became a livelihood for many tribal families.

source.title: Gond Art: Details about Gond Tribal Art and Painting of India

nations.name: Dayak
nations.lands: Borneo: Kalimantan (Indonesia), Sabah and Sarawak (Malaysia) and Brunei

facts.text: Dayak is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Borneo, by some estimates about 450 ethnolinguistic groups.
Dayak peoples share traditions of longhouse living and customary law known as adat.

nations.name: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung
nations.lands: Melbourne and surrounding lands, including the Birrarung (Yarra River), Victoria, Australia

facts.text: The Wurundjeri council was set up in 1985 by Wurundjeri descendants and gained Registered Aboriginal Party status for cultural heritage in 2008.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: In 2017 a Yarra River protection bill was the first legislation put before Victoria's parliament with a dual Aboriginal language title: Wilip-gin Birrarung murron, keep the Birrarung alive.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: iTaukei
nations.lands: Fiji

facts.text: The iTaukei Land Trust Board, set up in 1940, manages iTaukei land for its owners, whether a yavusa, mataqali or tokatoka.
The iTaukei Affairs Board, set up in 1944 as the Fijian Affairs Board, is the main advisory and coordinating body for iTaukei affairs, supporting village, tikina and provincial leaders.

nations.name: Kosraeans
nations.lands: Kosrae, an island state in the east of the Federated States of Micronesia, with the municipalities of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe

facts.text: Kosrae State has its own constitutional government, with a legislature elected by voters in the districts of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe.

source.title: Kosrae
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: In 2017 Kosraean elders proposed protecting Kosrae's mountain range, seen as the figure Mahkontowe, now the Mahkontowe Conservation Area under Kosrae State law.

nations.name: Moriori
nations.lands: Rēkohu and Rangihaute (the Chatham and Pitt Islands), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Moriori are the Indigenous people of Rēkohu and Rangihaute, the Chatham Islands, and are represented by the Hokotehi Moriori Trust.
The Hokotehi Moriori Trust takes part in key parts of the Rēkohu economy, such as fishing, farming and tourism.

nations.name: Gadigal
nations.lands: The southern side of Sydney Harbour (Port Jackson), from South Head to around Petersham, in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

facts.text: Descendants of the Eora still live in Sydney today and proudly use the name Eora.
The City of Sydney formally acknowledges the Gadigal of the Eora Nation as the traditional custodians of the place now called Sydney.

nations.name: Larrakia
nations.lands: The Darwin region, from Cox Peninsula in the west to Gunn Point in the north, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Larrakia Nation Aboriginal Corporation, set up in 1997, runs about 40 programs in Darwin, including the Larrakia Land and Sea Rangers.
Larrakia are the traditional owners of the Darwin region, with country reaching from Cox Peninsula in the west up to Gunn Point in the north.

nations.name: Marshallese
nations.lands: the atolls and islands of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including Majuro

facts.text: Waan Aelõñ in Majel, Canoes of the Marshall Islands, is a Majuro program that trains young Marshallese women and men in skills for a sustainable future.

source.title: Canoes of the Marshall Islands, Waan Aelõñ in Majel

facts.text: A Marshallese stick chart maps how ocean swells bend around islands, with cowrie shells for the islands, and is studied before a voyage rather than used at sea.

source.title: Stick Navigation Chart
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

nations.name: Kaurna
nations.lands: The Adelaide Plains of South Australia, from around Crystal Brook in the north, bounded by the Mount Lofty Ranges to the east, Australia

facts.text: In March 2018 Kaurna people were recognised as native title holders around Adelaide, the first positive native title determination over a capital city area.

source.title: Native Title Recognition For Kaurna People Over Adelaide Area

facts.text: Requests for Kaurna names and translations all go through Kaurna Warra Karrpanthi, an Aboriginal corporation.

source.title: Aboriginal people of South Australia: Kaurna

nations.name: Torres Strait Islanders
nations.lands: the islands of the Torres Strait between Cape York and Papua New Guinea, in Queensland, Australia, and the Northern Peninsula Area

facts.text: The Torres Strait Regional Authority, an Australian Government body set up on 1 July 1994, counts recognising and maintaining Torres Strait Islander Ailan Kastom among its functions.
Kala Lagaw Ya is the traditional language of the western and central Torres Strait islands, and Meriam Mir is the language of the eastern islands.

nations.name: Noongar
nations.lands: The south-west of Western Australia, including the Perth region, Australia

facts.text: Western Australia's settlement recognises the Noongar people as the traditional owners of the South-West, with about A$1.3 billion in land and other benefits.

source.title: All six South West Native Title Settlement Agreements registered

facts.text: The South West Native Title Settlement covers about 200,000 square kilometres and affects an estimated 40,000 Noongar people.

source.title: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council
source.publisher: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council

nations.name: Yolŋu
nations.lands: North-east Arnhem Land, including the Gove Peninsula, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Yolŋu elders founded Dhimurru Aboriginal Corporation to manage their land on the Gove Peninsula and the visitors who come to it.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

facts.text: The name Dhimurru means east wind, the wind that carries the monsoon rains and brings new life to the land.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

nations.name: Waikato-Tainui
nations.lands: The Waikato region of the North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui describes itself as a growing tribe of over 90,000 people, voyagers and pioneers like their ancestors.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui celebrate their identity as people of the Tainui waka and as protectors of the Kiingitanga movement.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

nations.name: Niueans
nations.lands: the island of Niue in the South Pacific, with villages such as Alofi, Mutalau and Toi

facts.text: Fale Tāoga Niue, home of the Niue National Museum, opened on 19 October 2018, the anniversary of the Niue Constitution Celebrations.
Niue's Vagahau Niue Act 2012 recognises Vagahau Niue as the official language of Niue and created the Niue Language Commission to protect it.

source.title: Vagahau Niue Act 2012
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Samoans
nations.lands: the Independent State of Samoa, on Upolu, Savai'i and nearby islands

facts.text: Women and master weavers have formed fine mat committees in their villages, and more young women, and some men, now weave the 'ie Samoa.

source.title: 'Ie Samoa, fine mat and its cultural value

facts.text: Samoa's 2021 census counted 16,082 people aged 21 and over who hold a matai, or chiefly, title, including 1,444 women.

source.title: Samoa Population and Housing Census 2021 Fact Sheet (Final Results, October 2022)

nations.name: Chuukese
nations.lands: Chuuk State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on the high islands of Chuuk Lagoon such as Weno, Tonoas, Uman and Fefan, and outlying atolls

facts.text: Chuuk's state constitution says existing Chuukese custom and tradition shall be respected, and lets traditional leaders hold formal roles in government.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Chuuk's constitution recognizes traditional rights over all reefs, tidelands and other submerged lands, including the water above them.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Palauans
nations.lands: the Republic of Palau in the western Pacific, with 16 states on Babeldaob, Koror and other islands

facts.text: Palauans still use the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon, a World Heritage site since 2012, for cultural purposes under a traditional governance system.
Palau's Council of Chiefs, made up of the highest traditional chiefs from each state, advises the President on traditional laws and customs.

nations.name: Gunantuna
nations.lands: the Gazelle Peninsula of New Britain Island, East New Britain Province, Papua New Guinea

facts.text: Diwarra pays for everyday things such as store goods and school fees, and sharing it out expresses ties between clans and individuals.

source.title: Gunantuna (Tolai people)
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

facts.text: In 2016 a Queensland gallery commissioned A Bit na Ta, a collaborative work made with the wider Tolai community whose music carries the rhythms of Tolai life from 1875 to 1975.

source.title: Art from Papua New Guinea Celebrated in Major QAG Exhibition
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

nations.name: Whanganui Iwi
nations.lands: The Whanganui River, from the mountains to the sea, North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui, the iwi river trust, was established in August 2014 with the signing of Ruruku Whakatupua.

source.title: Home | Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui

facts.text: Since 2017, New Zealand law has recognised the Whanganui River, Te Awa Tupua, as a legal person, with a guardian office that acts as its human face.

source.title: The Whanganui River (Te Awa Tupua)
source.publisher: OsloMet (Oslo Metropolitan University), River Rights project

nations.name: Ngāi Tahu
nations.lands: Te Waipounamu (the South Island), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: There are 18 Papatipu Rūnanga, local Ngāi Tahu councils, spread throughout Te Waipounamu, the South Island.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

facts.text: Ngāi Tahu means people of Tahu, and whakapapa, the ancestral link, binds all Ngāi Tahu whānau.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

nations.name: Nauruans
nations.lands: the island of Nauru, officially styled Naoero, in the central Pacific

facts.text: Nauru's government now presents the country as the Republic of Naoero on its official website.

source.title: The Government of the Republic of Naoero
source.publisher: Government of the Republic of Nauru

facts.text: In Nauru's 2021 census, 69 percent of residents aged 5 and over spoke only Nauruan at home, and another 25.3 percent spoke it with another language.

source.title: Nauru 2021 Population and Housing Census: Analytical Report

nations.name: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei
nations.lands: Central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei's shared affairs are looked after by their Trust and two subsidiaries: Whai Māia, the social arm, and Whai Rawa, the commercial arm.
Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei are the tangata whenua, the people of the land, of Te Kahu Tōpuni o Tuperiri in central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland).

nations.name: Refaluwasch
nations.lands: Saipan and other islands of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, a United States commonwealth in the western Pacific

facts.text: In December 2020 the Matawal Wóól Display Hall opened with photos and crafts made by students of the Tepengi Kkosch Refaluwasch culture program.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2021 Citizen Centric Report

facts.text: The Carolinian Affairs Office, created by the CNMI Constitution, advises the governor and works to protect and preserve the culture and traditions of Indigenous Carolinians.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2020 Citizen Centric Report

nations.name: Pohnpeians
nations.lands: Pohnpei State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on Pohnpei island and its outlying atolls

facts.text: Nan Madol, a World Heritage site since 2016, is traditionally owned and managed under the Nahnmwarki system, a chiefly institution that continues in Pohnpei today.

source.title: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia

facts.text: Pohnpei State's constitution protects the customs and traditions of Pohnpei's traditional kingdoms alongside its elected government.

source.title: Pohnpei
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Imazighen
nations.lands: North Africa (Tamazgha): Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt's Siwa oasis, with communities across the Sahel and in the diaspora

facts.text: After decades of campaigning, Tamazight was recognized as a national and official language in Algeria's Constitution in 2016.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Algeria
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Amazigh identity and the Amazigh language, Tamazight, have had official recognition in Morocco's Constitution since 2011.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Morocco
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Griqua
nations.lands: the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal provinces of South Africa

facts.text: Griqua communities live today in the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Early Griqua communities governed themselves through leaders called kaptyns, with magistrates drawn from leading families.

nations.name: Siwans
nations.lands: the oases of Siwa and El-Gara in Egypt's Western Desert, near the border with Libya

facts.text: A sense of Berber belonging has revived in Siwa this century; a letter of the Tifinagh alphabet, the Amazigh symbol, now names a bazaar below old Shali.

source.title: Siwa, the Berber oasis where cultures cross (An Atlas of Contemporary Egypt, 2023)

facts.text: Ten Siwan tribes speak Siwi, an eastern Amazigh (Berber) language, in the oases of Siwa and El-Gara.

source.title: Siwa, the Berber oasis where cultures cross (An Atlas of Contemporary Egypt, 2023)

nations.name: Khwe
nations.lands: north-eastern Namibia, north-western Botswana and southern Angola, and Platfontein near Kimberley in South Africa

facts.text: In South Africa, Khwe and !Xun communities live mainly at Platfontein, near Kimberley.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Khwe people in Namibia have their own Traditional Authority. As of 2025 the government had not recognized it, which Khwe say makes land and development issues harder to resolve.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Ogiek
nations.lands: highland forests of Kenya, especially the Mau Forest

facts.text: In December 2025 the African Court issued its first ever compliance decision, in the Ogiek case, finding that Kenya had not yet carried out its judgments.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Kenya
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2017 the African Court ruled for the Ogiek, its first ruling for an Indigenous people, and recognized Indigenous peoples as guardians of local ecosystems.

nations.name: Datooga
nations.lands: northern Tanzania, including the highlands near Mount Hanang in Manyara Region and the Lake Eyasi area

facts.text: Datooga and Hadza communities own more than 110,000 hectares of dryland forest protected through the Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape project.
With help from the NGO Ujamaa Community Resource Team, Barabaig communities in northern Tanzania gained grazing land held under collective title.

nations.name: Hai//om
nations.lands: north-central Namibia, in and around Etosha National Park and on resettlement farms in Kunene, Oshikoto and Oshana regions

facts.text: In July 2026 Namibia's Vice President opened a high-level meeting in Outjo with the Hai//om Traditional Authority on a development plan for Hai//om communities.

source.title: Government Reaffirms Commitment to Hai-//om Community Development, Vice President Lucia Witbooi (speech)

facts.text: Many Hai//om communities lived on lands that are now Etosha National Park and the surrounding regions, according to the Hai//om Community San Council.

source.title: Challenges Faced by the Hai//om San Marginalized Communities in Namibia: Challenges and Solutions
source.publisher: Cultural Survival (by the Hai//om Community San Council)

nations.name: Wodaabe
nations.lands: the Sahel of Niger, with communities in Chad, northern Cameroon and north-east Nigeria

facts.text: In 2008 thousands of Wodaabe herders attended the fourth General Assembly of the Woodaabe Pastoralists of Niger.

source.title: Oromo pastoralists visit Woodaabe General Assembly in Niger

facts.text: Cattle herding is the main livelihood of the Wodaabe, who move with the seasons across the Sahel.

nations.name: Konso
nations.lands: the Konso highlands of south-western Ethiopia

facts.text: The Konso built the dry-stone terraces of their highlands and still farm them; UNESCO lists the Konso Cultural Landscape as World Heritage.
The Konso raise stone steles to mark the handing of responsibility from the older generation to the younger, a living tradition.

nations.name: Kel Tamasheq
nations.lands: the Sahara and Sahel: northern Mali and Niger, southern Algeria and Libya, and northern Burkina Faso

facts.text: In Libya, the Fezzan region, including Ubari and Ghat, is traditional Kel Tamasheq territory, linked to communities across the borders in Niger and Algeria.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Libya
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

source.title: Endorois Welfare Council - Endorois Welfare Council for marginalized communities

nations.name: Yiaku

facts.text: Yiaku women and elders now lead language teaching and forest care, and growing youth involvement is strengthening the community.

source.title: Reviving Indigenous forest stewardship

source.title: Reviving Indigenous forest stewardship

nations.name: Anywaa
nations.lands: Gambella in western Ethiopia, along the Akobo, Alwaro, Openo (Baro) and Gilo rivers, and neighbouring South Sudan

facts.text: Anywaa activists helped found EMIPRO in 2022, the first legally registered Indigenous-led rights organization in Ethiopia.

source.title: “We Belong to This Land:” The Anywaa Peoples’ Fight for Survival, Dignity, and Recognition in Ethiopia

facts.text: The Anywaa are river farmers and fishers whose lives follow the Akobo, Alwaro, Openo (Baro) and Gilo rivers of Gambella.

source.title: “We Belong to This Land:” The Anywaa Peoples’ Fight for Survival, Dignity, and Recognition in Ethiopia

nations.name: Toubou
nations.lands: the Tibesti plateau of northern Chad, southern Libya along the Chad border, and northern Niger

facts.text: Toubou herders practise mobile pastoralism across a wide area stretching from northern Niger to Sudan.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Libya chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)

nations.name: Rifians
nations.lands: the Rif of northern and north-eastern Morocco, including Al Hoceima province

facts.text: In Morocco's 2024 census, 53.6% of people in Al Hoceima province said they use Tarifit, the language of the Irifiyen.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima

nations.name: Baka
nations.lands: forests of eastern and southern Cameroon, northern Gabon, and neighbouring parts of the Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic

facts.text: In Gabon, the Baka are one of nine Indigenous forest peoples, alongside the Babongo, Bakoya and others, each with its own language and culture.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Gabon chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Cameroon
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Sengwer
nations.lands: Cherangany Hills and Embobut Forest in Kenya's western highlands

facts.text: Sengwer society is organized around clans, each with its own roles, and elders guide decisions and teach younger generations.
Sengwer knowledge includes sustainable ways of hunting, gathering, beekeeping and caring for forest resources, which helps conserve biodiversity.

nations.name: Kabyles
nations.lands: Kabylia in north-eastern Algeria, with a large community in France

facts.text: Taqbaylit, the Kabyle language, is one of three Amazigh languages taught from bachelor's level to doctorate at Inalco in Paris.

source.title: Kabyle (Berber)
source.publisher: Inalco (Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales)

facts.text: Kabyles make up around half of Algeria's Amazigh population, centred on Kabylia in the north-east.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Algeria chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Mozabite
nations.lands: the M'Zab valley around Ghardaïa in the Algerian Sahara

facts.text: UNESCO credits the M'Zab with an ingenious system for capturing and sharing water which, with its palm groves, makes life work in a semi-desert.
The M'Zab valley habitat, built in the tenth century by the Ibadites around five ksour (fortified towns), survives intact and is UNESCO World Heritage.

nations.name: BaAka
nations.lands: forests between the Oubangui and Sangha rivers, in south-western Central African Republic and northern Republic of the Congo

facts.text: Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas credits BaAka knowledge of the forest as central to its research, conservation and tourism work.
The Central African Republic, home to many BaAka communities, ratified ILO Convention 169 on Indigenous peoples in 2010, the first African state to do so.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2021: Central African Republic
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
also: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Wewoka and Seminole County, Oklahoma, United States; earlier homelands in Florida

facts.text: The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is made up of fourteen bands, and its General Council seats two representatives from each band rather than from districts.

source.title: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma: Written Testimony to the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs
source.publisher: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma, via U.S. Senate Committee on Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Seminole Nation Language Program works to maintain, revitalize and carry forward the language and traditional ways of the Seminole people.

nations.name: Rappahannock Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds in Virginia, as described by the Tribe's environmental department

facts.text: The Tribe's environmental department says it coordinates the Return to the River youth program.

source.title: Department Of Environmental Services | Rappahannock Indian Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe dates its incorporation to 1921 as part of efforts to strengthen its government and seek recognition.

nations.name: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation
nations.lands: Guntersville, Alabama

facts.text: A January 2020 post describes a Word of the Month practice series, with a new calendar of practice planned for February.
In January 2020, the Nation announced a plan to highlight enrolled citizens' crafted items in its public posts.

source.title: Attention: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation Artisans - UCAN

nations.name: Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe
nations.lands: Akwesasne, on the St. Lawrence River in northern New York, United States; the wider Akwesasne community extends into Canada

facts.text: The Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Council is made up of three Chiefs, three Sub-Chiefs and a Tribal Clerk, with elections scheduled each year and set terms of office.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

facts.text: The Tribe describes its original homeland as northeastern New York State, reaching into southern Canada and Vermont.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

nations.name: Coharie Tribe
nations.lands: Harnett and Sampson Counties in southeastern North Carolina, where the Tribe locates its present community

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes the Coharie Intra-Tribal Council as representing Harnett and Sampson Counties.
The Tribe's history locates the present Coharie population in North Carolina's Harnett and Sampson Counties.

nations.name: Seneca Nation
nations.lands: Allegany, Cattaraugus and Oil Spring territories in Western New York, United States

facts.text: The Seneca Nation governs itself under a constitution established in 1848, with a 16-member Tribal Council drawn equally from the Cattaraugus and Allegany territories.

source.title: Seneca Nation of Indians - Official Website

facts.text: The Seneca Nation runs a language immersion program so students can hold conversations in Onöndowa’ga:’ Gawë:nö’, the Seneca language, alongside classes and online learning.

nations.name: Cherokee Nation
nations.lands: Tahlequah and a 14-county reservation area in Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in the Southeast

facts.text: Cherokee Nation governs through legislative, executive and judicial branches and serves people across a 14-county reservation area.
Written Cherokee uses a syllabary, not an alphabet, with 85 distinct characters; Cherokee Nation teaches it through an immersion school and a master-apprentice program.

nations.name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
nations.lands: The Qualla Boundary in western North Carolina, United States, beside the Great Smoky Mountains

facts.text: As a sovereign nation, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its own laws, holds its own elections and runs its own government and institutions.

source.title: Home - Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians

facts.text: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its home on the 56,000-acre Qualla Boundary, next to Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

source.title: NC Tribal Communities | NC DOA
source.publisher: North Carolina Department of Administration, Commission of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Seminole Tribe of Florida
nations.lands: Big Cypress, Brighton, Fort Pierce, Hollywood, Immokalee and Tampa reservations in Florida, United States

facts.text: The Tribal Council, with a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and representatives from each reservation, is the chief governing body of the Seminole Tribe of Florida.
Adding the Tampa and Immokalee reservations brought the Seminole Tribe of Florida's federal trust lands to more than 90,000 acres.

nations.name: Southeastern Mvskoke Nation
nations.lands: Near Troy in Alabama; its history describes organization around Pike and Coffee Counties.

facts.text: The Nation presents its language page as a small learning resource for Tribal members and other Mvskokes.
Its introduction locates the Nation near Troy in Alabama.

nations.name: Delaware Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Bartlesville, Oklahoma, United States; homelands along the Delaware River

facts.text: The Delaware Tribe of Indians is a federally recognized tribe of the Lenape people, headquartered in Bartlesville, Oklahoma.
The Tribe's online Lenape Talking Dictionary holds about 15,380 words, along with recorded stories and songs, and is still growing.

source.title: Language Revitalization - Delaware Tribe of Indians

pronounce.publisher: Delaware Tribe of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Sappony
nations.lands: the High Plains Indian Settlement along the North Carolina-Virginia boundary, including Person County, North Carolina, and Halifax County, Virginia, as described by Sappony

facts.text: Sappony describes committees addressing education, cultural preservation and economic development.
Sappony's governance page describes a council with one elected representative from each of the settlement's seven families.

nations.name: The Chickasaw Nation
nations.lands: Thirteen counties in south-central Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee

facts.text: The Chickasaw Nation's three-department government was reestablished with the ratification of its 1983 Constitution.
The Chickasaw language revitalization program began in 2007, and its master-apprentice program pairs learners with fluent Chickasaw speakers.

nations.name: Catawba Nation
nations.lands: York County, South Carolina, near Rock Hill, with a service area that includes North Carolina, United States

facts.text: After a 20-year effort, a land claim settlement on November 20, 1993 brought the Catawba Indian Nation federal recognition.
The Catawba Nation has over 3,300 enrolled citizens and continues to grow.

nations.name: Haliwa-Saponi Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Meadows area at present-day Hollister, North Carolina; the Tribe locates its government there without defining territorial boundaries in this source

facts.text: The Tribe describes Red Earth as a program for all ages to learn about Haliwa-Saponi history and cultural practices.

source.title: Cultural Classes - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

facts.text: The Tribal School's stated mission combines academics, technology and community involvement with American Indian culture.

source.title: Haliwa Saponi Tribal School: Quality Education - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

nations.name: Waccamaw Siouan Tribe
nations.lands: Bladen and Columbus Counties in southeastern North Carolina, near Green Swamp

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council elected by the membership and an Elders Review Committee.
The Tribe's introduction places its communities mainly in Bladen and Columbus Counties, North Carolina, near Green Swamp.

nations.name: Onondaga Nation
nations.lands: Onondaga Nation territory south of Syracuse, central New York, United States

facts.text: In the Haudenosaunee Grand Council, the Onondaga Fire Keepers present an issue, and debate goes on until they can announce that all are of One Mind, a decision by consensus.
The Onondaga Nation is still governed by its traditional government, with fourteen Chiefs and their Clan Mothers serving as caretakers of the land.

nations.name: Shinnecock Indian Nation
nations.lands: In and around the Town of Southampton on the eastern end of Long Island, New York, United States

facts.text: On October 1, 2010, the Shinnecock Indian Nation was formally recognized by the United States as the 565th federally recognized tribe.
The Shinnecock Indian Nation has over 1,589 enrolled tribal members.

nations.name: Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia
nations.lands: southeastern Virginia along the Nottoway River; the Tribe's Community House & Interpretive Center is in Capron

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes the Nottoway as Iroquoian speakers of southeastern Virginia.

source.title: Tribal History - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

facts.text: The Tribe says its Community House & Interpretive Center formally opened in Capron on May 5, 2012.

source.title: Community House & Interpretive Center - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

nations.name: Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina
nations.lands: Along the Lumbee River in Robeson, Hoke, Cumberland and Scotland counties, North Carolina, United States, centered on Pembroke

facts.text: The Lumbee Tribe became fully federally recognized by the United States on December 18, 2025.
The Lumbee Tribe describes its people, the People of the Dark Water, as entrepreneurial and strongly focused on education.

nations.name: Oneida Indian Nation
nations.lands: Central New York, United States

facts.text: Oneida Indian Nation Members learn Onyota’a:ká:, the Oneida language, through intensive courses, a preschool curriculum, e-books, smartphone apps and an Oneida language keyboard.
During the American Revolution, Oneidas fought alongside the colonists and carried corn to feed General Washington's starving soldiers; the Nation honors them as America's first allies.

nations.name: Osage Nation
nations.lands: Osage Nation Reservation, northeastern Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Pawhuska

facts.text: The Osage Minerals Council, an elected body of eight members, is part of the Osage Nation's government.
Since 2006 the Osage Nation has governed itself under a constitution with separate executive, legislative and judicial branches.

nations.name: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Standing Rock Reservation, across North Dakota and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: Today Yanktonai Dakota communities live mostly on the North Dakota side of Standing Rock, and Lakota communities mostly on the South Dakota side.
The Standing Rock Tribal Council has a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary and 14 council members, all elected by tribal members for four-year terms.

source.title: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Pawnee, Oklahoma, United States; ancestral homeland on the central Plains

facts.text: The Pawnee Business Council is the supreme governing body of the Pawnee Nation, acting within the nation's Constitution and federal law.
The Pawnee Nation is made up of four bands: the Čawî’ (Grand), Kitkahaki (Republican), Pitahawirata (Tappage) and Skidi (Wolf).

source.title: Pawnee History | Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska
nations.lands: Fifteen-county service area across Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe serves its people across a fifteen-county service area in Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, set up by the Ponca Restoration Act.
The Ponca Restoration Act, signed by President George H. W. Bush, restored federal recognition to the Ponca Tribe of Nebraska.

nations.name: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Cheyenne River Reservation, central South Dakota, United States; headquarters in Eagle Butte

facts.text: The tribe is governed by a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer and fifteen council members, with headquarters in Eagle Butte.

source.title: Cheyenne River Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Cheyenne River Reservation holds about 1.45 million trust acres in Ziebach and Dewey counties in central South Dakota.

source.title: Cheyenne River Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
nations.lands: Reservation along the Kansas and Nebraska border, United States

facts.text: The tribe is governed by two bodies, a General Council and an Executive Committee.

source.title: Welcome to the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

source.title: Welcome to the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

nations.name: Citizen Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Headquartered in Shawnee, Oklahoma, United States, with citizens around the world

facts.text: In July 2026 the Citizen Potawatomi Nation signed the articles of confederation for the Potawatomi Confederacy.
The Citizen Potawatomi Nation Constitution dates from 1938 and was amended in 1985 and again in 2007.

nations.name: Sac and Fox Nation
nations.lands: Central Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Stroud

facts.text: The Sac and Fox Nation supports learning Sauk through an interactive language website and a concise Sauk dictionary.
The Sac and Fox Nation was the first tribe to take on self-governance within the Indian Health Service.

nations.name: Forest County Potawatomi
nations.lands: Forest County, northern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Forest County Potawatomi Language and Culture Department works to keep the Bodwéwadmi language and traditions alive, with classes during the school year.
The Forest County Potawatomi Cultural Center, Library and Museum provides an important link to the community's past.

nations.name: Red Lake Nation
also: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Red Lake Reservation, northern Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Red Lake tribal government holds full sovereignty over its reservation, subject only to the federal government.

source.title: Red Lake Nation - Home of the Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians

facts.text: English is a second language for many Red Lake members who are middle-aged and older, including some on the Tribal Council, and many others speak or understand Ojibwe.

nations.name: Kiowa Tribe
nations.lands: Southwestern Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The Kiowa Tribe commits to protecting its sovereignty and to preserving and advocating for Kiowa culture and language.

source.title: Kiowa Tribe - Tribe, Native American, Native, Tribe

facts.text: The Kiowa Language Department runs a credentialed teacher training program to prepare new Kiowa language teachers.

source.title: Blackfeet Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Blackfeet Nation describes itself as a nation of 17,321 members.

nations.name: Oglala Sioux Tribe

facts.text: The Pine Ridge Reservation, home of the Oglala Sioux Tribe, covers about 2.1 million acres across Oglala Lakota, Jackson and Bennett counties in South Dakota.

source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
nations.lands: Fort Peck Reservation, northeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Poplar

facts.text: Members of the Fort Peck Tribal Executive Board, except the secretary-accountant, are elected at-large every two years.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes

facts.text: The Fort Peck Reservation in northeastern Montana includes more than two million acres of land.
